definition: Remorse is a feeling of guilt about one’s actions. In this packet, it refers to guilt or remorse felt after drinking alcohol.

provenance.scope: Source record C119114; pinned source text

reasons: The opening sentence is too general: the packet supports guilt or remorse specifically after drinking alcohol, not remorse in general as “a feeling of guilt about one’s actions.”
The packet is an AUDIT item/instrument prompt, so the definition should not present a broader standalone psychological sense unless supported by the source text.
The second sentence is only partially supported and should stay tightly tied to the drinking-after-alcohol context rather than implying a general packet-specific meaning.

The packet does not provide a general definition of “remorse” as “a feeling of guilt about one’s actions”; it only contains a questionnaire item referring to “a feeling of guilt or remorse after drinking.”
While the second sentence (“it refers to guilt or remorse felt after drinking alcohol”) is supported by the AUDIT item, the first sentence includes an unsupported generalization about remorse.
